This is the first stage, and the first command: the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone, but the ruling is for all believers. Because the address begins with:

Yā ayyuhā al-Nabiyyu (65:1) ("O Prophet").

And the command begins thus:

Idhā ............ al-Nisā' (65:1) "When you divorce women..." It is known that this command has great importance with God, and for this reason the impression is given that it should be taken with the utmost seriousness. This is an important command. Allah addresses His Prophet specially, saying: take this command and convey it to the people. This is a psychological manner and a method of the highest order of emphasis.

Idhā ṭallaqtum ............ li-'iddatihinna (65:1) "When you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period ('iddah)." In determining the meaning of this verse, there is a sound hadith in Bukhari Sharif. Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated from Layth, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه), who said: I had a wife whom I divorced while she was in her menses. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became very angry. Then he said: "He should take her back, keep her as his wife until she becomes pure from menses, then she becomes menstruating again, and then becomes pure when the period of menses ends. Now, if he wishes to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure and before he has touched her. This is the 'iddah for which Allah has commanded." Muslim has also narrated it, but his words are: "This is the 'iddah for which Allah has commanded women to be divorced."

This shows that the occurrence of divorce has a specified time. Therefore it is not permissible for a man to divorce his wife whenever he wishes, unless his wife is already in a state of purity (ṭuhr) and he has not touched her during that purity. Some narrations mention another case in which divorce may be given: that the woman is clearly pregnant. The divine wisdom in this is that divorce is thus postponed to a specified time, and when the man is inclined to divorce, it cannot be done immediately. In practice the divorce is postponed, and the benefit is that if there is a matter of sudden anger, it cools down, and during this period relations between the parties may be set right. Also, if she is pregnant, time may pass in ascertaining the pregnancy. Sometimes a person may refrain from divorce because of the pregnancy itself. When the pregnancy becomes known, in this case, if he divorces, it will be known that he has decided to divorce after careful thought. "That divorce be given in a state of purity in which he has not gone to his wife." This is because in that case the possibility of pregnancy is less. And the condition that "he first ascertain that there is no pregnancy" is so that he knows whether the wife is pregnant.

This is the first effort to prevent the husband from striking at the foundation of the family, and the pickaxe that strikes at the building of the family is stopped, or an attempt is made to stop it.

But this does not mean that if a person divorces without regard to these legal instructions, the divorce does not take effect. Whenever anyone divorces, the divorce takes effect. But to divorce in this manner is disliked (makruh). The wrath of Allah and His Messenger will descend upon such a person. (And this is called "bid'ī divorce" (ṭalāq bid'ī)), and for a true believer it is sufficient that he avoid it and act in accordance with the command of Allah.

Wa-aḥṣū al-'iddah (65:1) "Count the waiting period precisely." So that by not counting it, the woman observing 'iddah does not have the period extended, and so that, after completing the 'iddah, if she wishes to marry another husband, she does not have to wait without necessity. Or, if the period is counted short, the purposes for which the period exists are not fulfilled, namely the certainty of the purity of the womb for the protection of lineage. After this, detailed rulings on observing 'iddah follow. And the matter is entrusted to Allah's watchfulness and God-consciousness.

Wa-ittaqū Allāh ............ mubayyinah (65:1) "And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality." This is the first warning after the first call. Expelling women from their houses, or their leaving on their own, has been entrusted to God-consciousness, that in this matter you should fear God. It is said "do not expel them from *their* houses," although the houses belong to the husbands; but since they have the right to reside there and Allah has made their residence there obligatory, these houses of the husbands have been called *their* houses. Indeed, there is only one case in which they may leave the houses, or may be removed: if they commit an open indecency. If they commit fornication, they shall be removed for the prescribed punishment (ḥadd). Or if they become a source of harm to the husband's relatives. Or sometimes there may be disobedience and abusive speech toward the husband, because keeping the woman in the husband's house means that opportunities are provided for both to become inclined toward reconciliation, and that feelings of love have opportunities to work, and the memories of shared life can do their work; in such a way that the woman is physically distant from the husband yet within his sight. In this state there are possibilities of setting matters right between the two. If, while residing in the husband's house, she commits fornication, or indecency and abusive speech, or harms him and his household, then it appears there is no possibility of achieving the purposes intended by keeping her there. Therefore her remaining here will now only cause further bitterness, and there will be more hostility between the parties.

Wa-tilka ............ nafsah (65:1) "These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged his own soul." This is the second warning given to those who do not act upon Islam's law of divorce, because it is Allah Himself who enforces His commands and supervises their observance. If someone is a believer, he cannot cross the limits whose guardian is Allah. This is clear destruction and ruin. "Whoever transgresses the limits set by Allah has wronged himself." This is because the armies of Allah stand upon the limits of Allah. Then, this person, by wronging his wife, wrongs himself, since both were created from a single soul.

Lā tadrī ............ amran (65:1) "You do not know; perhaps after this Allah will bring about some circumstance." This is a deeply effective reminder. Who knows the matters hidden behind the veil of the future? Or who knows the decree of Allah and the wisdom for which the 'iddah has been prescribed, and why it has been ordained that they remain in the houses? This is an assurance of their hope and good expectation. Sometimes great good emerges from it. Sometimes circumstances suddenly change, misunderstandings are removed and agreement arises. The decree of Allah is always in motion; within it change occurs constantly; new events keep appearing. Therefore submitting to the commands of Allah is the best course, and there is good in fearing Allah.

Sometimes temporary circumstances overwhelm the human soul, and a person becomes compelled by present conditions, and the doors of the future seem closed to him. So he remains compelled in the filth of present conditions. He thinks that he must remain as he is now; this state will continue, present conditions will always be his companions, and present shadows will keep pursuing him. This is a psychological prison in which a person imprisons himself with his own hands, and sometimes it breaks the limbs.

But reality is not so. The decree of Allah mocks circumstances. Circumstances keep changing. "Constancy is only for change in this world." Sometimes after difficulties there come circumstances that people cannot even imagine. After hardship there is always ease. After constriction there is expansion, and Allah's splendor is new every day. All creation is in His hand.

Allah wills that the thought of this remain permanently in people's consciousness, so that they stay hopeful and keep their eyes fixed upon Allah, that He may remove difficulties at any moment. Changes of circumstance take no time, so the human mind too should keep its doors open to this, and should not close its mind out of despair. In the coming moment a revolution may take place.

Lā tadrī ............ amran (65:1) "You do not know that Allah may bring about, after this, some reconciliation."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 65, verse 2:

فاذا بلغن ............................ قدرا (56 : 3) (56 : 2۔ 3) "O Prophet! When you (people) divorce women, divorce them for their 'iddah (waiting period), and count the 'iddah exactly, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about some new situation afterwards." (The verse continues:) "So when they reach their term, either retain them in good manner or part with them in good manner, and call to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah. This is what is enjoined upon whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever puts his trust in Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah accomplishes His purpose. Allah has already set a measure for everything."

This is the second stage and its ruling. The 'iddah is completed, and as long as the woman has not come out of the 'iddah, the husband retains the right of return (raj'ah), and merely by returning she becomes his wife again. It should be remembered that we have already mentioned the various periods of 'iddah earlier. This is imsak (retention). Or, if he does not pronounce a further (second or third) divorce and the woman becomes ba'in (irrevocably separated), that is, she is separated by one or two divorces, then she becomes free. After that, if the husband wishes, he may conclude a fresh marriage with her with her consent. But if he returns to her or separates from her, the command is that he should deal with her in accordance with what is ma'ruf (customary good conduct). It is also forbidden to return to her merely to harass her. For example, he divorces the woman once, then returns to her before she completes the full 'iddah, then divorces her again, and then she begins a three-month 'iddah and, before it ends, he returns again and divorces her once more. Thus her 'iddah is prolonged up to nine months. This is causing harm to the woman. The meaning is that if he intends to keep her, he should return to her properly, and it should not be that he returns to her and keeps her suspended so that the poor woman is compelled to pay ransom. When this surah was revealed, such situations were occurring in Arab society, and it always happens when the fear of Allah departs from people's hearts. In both conditions, whether of companionship or separation, the fear of Allah is the best guarantor. Moreover, at the time of separating from a woman, abuse, harshness, harsh speech or beating is not ma'ruf. The ma'ruf way is to send her off with decency. It is also possible that the two may have to live together again, and in that case bad memories should not come between them. Thus bitter and unpleasant memories, harsh words or taunts should not stand in the way of re-establishing relations. This is the great educational lesson of Islam: that even in such difficult and bitter circumstances, it compels a person to adopt a dignified conduct.

Now, whether it is separation or return, in both situations the establishment of testimony is necessary. Two just witnesses should stand upon it, so that no doubt arises in any matter, that people should know about the divorce but not know about the return. Suspicions would spread among people, and people would gossip that so-and-so's wife is divorced. Whereas Islam's policy is that people's hearts and tongues should both be clean regarding the husband and wife. The majority of jurists are of the view that testimony is not necessary for return or separation. Some jurists consider it necessary, but both views hold that testimony should definitely be established so that it may be useful when needed, and so that people do not get an opportunity to gossip. Therefore, after this explanation, several instructions are given and reminders are made:

واقیموا ................ للہ (56 : 2) "And establish the testimony for Allah." Because this is an important matter, and giving testimony for Allah is obligatory upon the witness. Allah commands its establishment. It is He who also commands its performance, and He will also give reward for it. In this matter, the dealing is with God, not with the husband, not with the wife, and not with people.

ذلکم ........................ الاخر (56 : 2) "This is what you are admonished with, for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day." Those addressed in these verses were believers, and all of them believed in Allah and the Day of Judgment. Allah tells them that these are very important matters. If they have truly believed in Allah and the Last Day, then they should respect these divine commands. This will be the criterion for their faith, and this will be the measure of their claim of faith.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 65, verse 3:

﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out [of difficulties], and will provide for him from where he does not expect.﴾ (56:3 in the Urdu numbering) He will deliver them from the hardships of this world and the Hereafter, and will provide them sustenance from sources they never imagined. This is a general decree and a permanent reality. Yet here these principles are applied to the rulings of divorce. The indication is that these rulings should be implemented fully and completely. Fear of Allah is a principle most effective in such matters. The fear of Allah is the best guardian for a person; otherwise people find their own loopholes in legal codes. Only taqwa (God-consciousness) can keep a person on the path of right action.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose.﴾ In such matters there is great scope for intrigue, and sometimes one must scheme to counter a scheme. Here it is said: do not engage in such schemes; rely upon Allah, and for those who rely upon Allah, He is sufficient. Allah carries out His affairs; whatever decisions He has made come to pass. Therefore, relying upon Allah and His decrees, since He is the great Power who does what He wills, is a major means of success.

This verse is general. The purpose is to instill in the hearts the correct state of faith and reliance, with regard to Allah's will and Allah's decree. However, since this general matter has come here in connection with divorce, it also points specifically to divorce, because it too is one of Allah's decrees.

﴿Allah has set a measure for everything.﴾ Everything is measured by Him, under His control; every event has its place and its station. Its circumstances, its causes and its results are created by Him. Nothing comes into existence on its own, nor do these affairs proceed merely as though someone were steering them. This entire universe, the human self, and all the events of human life emerge as a consequence of this great reality, that is, in accordance with the divine decree. (We have discussed this under the verse ...)

(The topic was discussed in detail under the phrase "and created everything and determined it a measure," see Surah al-Furqan: 2.) The point here is that this divorce, this reconciliation, the waiting period ('iddah), the giving of testimony, the discharge of testimony, and all such rulings are determined by Allah, and they unfold in the same way as the divine practice (sunnah Ilahiyyah) unfolds in the universe. In this way, a person understands these matters as the decisions of Allah are made.

Surah At-Talaq (65), verse 4, with Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation)

Quranic text: "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubt, then their 'iddah is three months, and likewise for those who have not yet menstruated. And for women who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair." This is the command of Allah which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge his reward.

These verses specify the period of 'iddah for women who do not menstruate and are not pregnant. That is, women whose menstruation has ceased, or whose periods have not come due to illness or because of young age. This is because the period of 'iddah mentioned earlier in Surah al-Baqarah was for women who do menstruate, whether the word qur' (قروء) is taken to mean three cycles of menstruation or three periods of purity; this is a jurisprudential difference of opinion. As for women whose periods have stopped, or never came, or never began, their situation was ambiguous as to how they should observe 'iddah. Therefore, it was made equal to the period of menstruating women. As for pregnant women, their period is until childbirth. Whether this period after divorce is long or short, although the period for purification after postpartum bleeding (nifas) is forty days. But the 'iddah was prescribed so that it could be seen whether the woman had a child in her womb. Now, a pregnant divorcee is separated from her husband upon giving birth, so there is no need to wait after that, and after childbirth she cannot be taken back in return, only a new marriage contract is possible. Allah has set a measure for everything, so there is wisdom behind every command.

That was the command; now, advice, lessons and wisdoms.

"And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair." Human beings naturally desire that their affairs be made easy for them. It is a great blessing that Allah creates ease for people in some of His matters, so that they face no difficulty, no punishment, no torment, no hardship and no burden. They feel ease according to their own measure and understanding. They find their actions and affairs easy in movement and work, they find it easy to accomplish tasks and obtain their results, and they remain in that state until they meet Allah. This divorce too is among the matters in which Allah has created ease. (In Christianity and Hinduism, divorce did not exist at all.)

This is the command of Allah which He has sent down to you. This is a further sensitisation: be serious. This command is Allah's; He has sent it down upon those who are believers. Therefore, acting upon it is a requirement of faith, and the implementation of this command is connected with Allah.

Once again, people are directed towards God-consciousness (taqwa), upon which great emphasis has been placed in this surah, although it is a surah of rulings.

And whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him, and will remove his misdeeds from him, and will magnify his reward. The first point was that Allah would create ease, and now that He will forgive his sins and increase his reward. Thus it is a reciprocal bounty, and a benefit that affects the human being. This is a general command, applicable to divorce and all other matters; but here the intention is to cast its shade upon matters of divorce, so that people may be filled with awareness of Allah's watchfulness, and may perceive Allah's grace: that if any task appears difficult to them, Allah will make it easy, and if any shortcoming occurs in it, He will grant forgiveness.

This is the final statement in which the question of residence in the home is taken up, along with the matter of maintenance (nafaqah) during the waiting period ('iddah), whatever its duration. The principle is that the husband should provide his wife with whatever kind of accommodation is available. It should be of the kind in which he himself lives, and he should provide as much as his financial position allows. In their dealings there should be no intention to cause harm. The accommodation should not be made cramped, nor should her honour be diminished, nor should she be wronged in other matters, such as speech.

Maintenance for pregnant women is mentioned specifically, although maintenance is obligatory for women observing every kind of 'iddah. This is because the period of pregnancy can sometimes be long, and one might think that maintenance is due only for three months. Or, if the child is born very soon after the divorce, one might suppose that maintenance is due only for a longer period. Therefore, it has been defined: maintenance continues until the legally prescribed 'iddah period ends, whether it is short or long.

After this, the details of the matter of breastfeeding are given. Breastfeeding is not made the mother's obligation without compensation. As long as she is nursing their common child, she has the right to be paid for this service, so that she can sustain herself and the child's milk also continues. These are the concessions the Islamic legal system grants to the mother. Along with these concessions, both parties are advised to decide matters concerning the child through mutual consultation, and to keep the child's welfare in view, since the child is a trust between them. Let it not be that the failure of their married life becomes a calamity for the child, who has no fault in it.

This is the good conduct to which both are invited. If they adopt a harsh attitude towards one another and cannot agree about nursing and its compensation, then the child must still be nursed. Someone else will nurse him.

“﴿So another woman shall nurse [the child] for him﴾” (56:6). Neither will the mother be objected to, nor will the child be deprived of milk and left to perish. This is because their common life has dissolved, and they then dealt harshly with one another, while the child bore no fault in it.

Following this, the principles of maintenance (nafaqah) are determined. In it, there is facilitation of one another, cooperation, and dealing with justice and kindness. Harshness and obstinacy are not permissible in it. If Allah has granted someone abundance, then he should spend according to his abundance, in both residence and livelihood, and in the wages for breastfeeding. And for one whose financial condition is not good, there is no harm if a limited wage is taken from him. For Allah burdens no one except to the extent of what He has given him, and no person can spend beyond his wealth and resources, for wealth is only that which Allah gives to someone.

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ (65:7).

During the period of breastfeeding, both parties are given the hope that they should keep their hope and desire for good circumstances from Allah alone:

﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾ (65:7). Ease after hardship and abundance after difficulty are all the work of Allah. Therefore both of them should turn towards Allah alone. They should attach their hopes to Allah alone; He is the Giver, He is the one who grants expansiveness, and contraction and expansion, difficulty and facility, harshness and gentleness, are all in His control.

Up to here, all the rules of divorce and the legal arrangements for the effects arising as a result of divorce have been explained, and a clear solution has been given for all the consequences. And all the rubble of that collapsed household, even its dust, has been cleared away so that hearts do not become dust-laden, bitterness is removed from hearts, and the spouses, forgetting the past, begin a new life afresh; the previous enmity is completely erased, and whatever anguish was within hearts has been ended so that no fresh agitation arises.

Whispers and lowness have been removed from hearts, and the parties have been made capable of establishing social relations anew with one another. If the husband spends generously on his divorced wife or on his own child, he is told that by this expenditure he will not become poor; and the wife too is told that if she takes a lesser compensation for breastfeeding the child, she will not become richer by it, so she too should not adopt a harsh attitude regarding her former husband and her own child. It is Allah who grants expansion after difficulties. The provision of the Hereafter is of greater importance than the provision of this world.

Regarding the bitterness and ill-feeling that arise as a result of divorce, the command is given that these should be forgotten, and a better future should be hoped for from Allah. Whatever has happened was decreed. Now, from here on, they should deal with one another in a recognized manner (ma'ruf), and have fear of God.

This is a complete remedy, these are effective admonitions, and these repeated, thrice-emphasized exhortations, that you deal with one another in what is recognized (ma'ruf), are all the best guarantee for removing the effects of this unpleasant event. Nothing other than a sense of conscience and fear of God can guarantee reform (islah dhat al-bayn) among Muslims. If, with fear of God removed, only a legal battle breaks out between the parties, its outcome is nothing but bitterness. Some rulings are so gentle that bitterness is removed by them themselves, which cannot be counted through any law. Accordingly, through this moral command it is stated that women should not be given any kind of hardship, and in this regard the fear of God should be adopted. It is Allah who knows every hidden and apparent thing, and for the God-fearing, Allah is the giver of reward in both this world and the Hereafter. Especially the matter of provision is in the hand of Allah alone, which has been mentioned repeatedly in this surah, because provision and interest are the very matters over which disputes arise, and after divorce most quarrels are over financial matters and interests.

After the conclusion of the matters of divorce, now the matter of the entire religion is mentioned with a historical attitude: that if you violate the laws of divorce, then in history many nations turned away from the messengers' mission and the religion they presented, but their end was not good. Now too this religion and this Shari'ah are being given to you in this form, which is a blessing; appreciate it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 65, verse 8:

وكأين من قرية ........................ رزقا (11) (65: 8 to 11)

"How many a town has rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, and We called it to a severe reckoning and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the consequence of its deeds, and the end of its affair was loss upon loss. Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment (in the Hereafter). So fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger who recites to you the clear verses of Allah, so that he may bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous work, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly made excellent provision for him."

This is a long warning, with detailed scenes. Then, to those who believed and to whom the light of faith was granted, it was told that this is a great favour of Allah upon them, and its reward they will receive on the Day of Resurrection, and the reward of the Resurrection is in truth the goodly provision (rizq husn).

History: those who did not submit to the Messenger and disobeyed, it has been Allah's way (sunnah) to seize the disobedient.

وكأين .................... عذابا نكرا (65: 8)

"How many a town has rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, and We called it to a severe reckoning and punished it with a terrible punishment." The detail of their seizure, the severe reckoning, the severe punishment and the picture of the evil end was this.

﴿So they tasted ....................  loss﴾ (56 : 9) "They tasted the consequence of their deeds, and the end of their affair was nothing but loss." Allah has prepared a severe punishment for them (in the Hereafter). And the depiction of this punishment was as follows:

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 65, verse 10:

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment.﴾ (65:10) These details of the punishment and its evil end are given so that the fear of disobeying Allah's commands remains upon human nerves for a long time. It is the style of the Quran to describe the scenes of Allah's punishment in great detail and at length.

It is necessary to reflect upon this warning: nations that disobeyed were seized one after another, and the mention of this seizure comes here in the context of disobedience to the commands and laws. Thus, the laws and commands of divorce are also connected with the Sunnah of Allah (sunnat Ilahiyyah, the established way of Allah). By this, it is intended to convey the impression that the laws of divorce are not merely a legal matter, but that they are connected with the collective system of the Muslim ummah. In this regard, the whole ummah will also be held accountable, and if these laws are violated, the punishment of Allah will come upon the whole ummah. The whole ummah is answerable for the consequences of opposing the laws of divorce and the other commands of the Islamic system, because the responsibility for running the Islamic system and the Islamic manhaj (method) is collective. Not only will those who violate it deserve the punishment of Allah, but the whole village and the whole ummah will be held accountable, which tolerates violation in the organisation of its system of life. This religion has come precisely so that it may be obeyed and implemented, and that it may dominate the whole of life. Thus, here the whole ummah has been declared disobedient; if the responsibility for establishing the Islamic system were individual, the whole ummah would not have been destroyed.

These towns were declared disobedient, and they tasted the evil consequence of their deeds, and in the end they were afflicted with loss. And this punishment was given to them in this very world. The punishment was given to towns, nations and communities that rejected the Islamic manhaj. We also bear witness, and our forefathers also bore witness, that nations which disobeyed the laws of marriage and divorce were punished. They lived through corruption, disorder, poverty, famine, oppression, restlessness, extreme insecurity and a life of fear in which there was no peace or tranquillity, and even today we see several such nations on this earth.

This punishment is in addition to that which awaits those disobedient ones who violated the commands of Allah and who rebelled against the Islamic system. Allah says:

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment.﴾ (65:10) And Allah is most truthful.

This religion is a manhaj of life and has a collective system of life, the details of which we have given in Surah As-Saff. Its purpose is to form a community that has a system, and to transform the life of that community and society. Therefore, this whole community will be held accountable regarding this religion. And this community will not violate these commands in such a way that this threat, which was given to the earlier nations who disobeyed the command of Allah, would apply to it.

In this warning and its lengthy scenes, the address is to people of understanding who believe, and the proof of their understanding is precisely that they have believed: fear Allah, who has sent down to you this reminder.

﴿Indeed, Allah has sent down to you a reminder.﴾ (65:10) And this reminder, a definite one, is present with you. The Messenger is the embodiment of the reminder. The whole person of the Messenger has been brought in grammatical terms as an apposition (badal) of "al-Dhikr."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 65, verse 11:

﴿A Messenger who recites to you the clear revelations of Allah﴾ (65:11)

This is an extremely profound point deserving of attention, and there are many lessons in it. The Dhikr (Remembrance, i.e. the Qur'an) that the Messenger has brought to people has reached them from within the personality of the Messenger of Allah. He was Sadiq (truthful) and Amin (trustworthy), and he conveyed the entire Dhikr to them, as though this Dhikr reached them directly from Allah. The person of the Messenger did not conceal any part of it.

The second point is that this verse describes the person of the Messenger as Dhikr, showing that the Messenger's person is entirely Dhikr. The Messenger is, as it were, the embodiment of Dhikr, and he is the living Qur'an. Hadrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) pointed to this when she said:

كان خلقه القرآن ("His character was the Qur'an"). He had the Qur'an in his heart, and he presented the Qur'an in his practical life.

Alongside Dhikr, the believers were promised light, guidance, righteous deeds and the blessings of Paradise, and it was stated that the provisions in the Gardens will be far more honoured than the provisions of this world; they are most excellent.

Once again the subject of provision is raised, and it is explained that the provision of this world is given to everyone, whereas the true provision is the provision of the Hereafter, while for the believers there is also a promise of good provision (Rizq Hasan) in this world.

And finally, the whole universe is brought into view, which is vast beyond wonder. Thus the subject of this entire surah, namely the laws of divorce, is linked with Allah's system of qadar (divine decree) and with the law of Allah's natural order governing this vast universe.

Allah is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them, so that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge (56:21). [Note: the Urdu passage quotes this verse as "al-Talaq 65:12" context; the translation below follows the Urdu text as given.]

Allah is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them, so that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.

We have not yet acquired complete knowledge of the seven heavens: how great their distances and intervals are. Likewise, we do not have knowledge of the seven earths. This earth on which we live would be one of them, and the rest are within the knowledge of Allah. It may also be understood that this earth is of the same kind as the heavens, in its composition and its characteristics. We do not, for now, wish to apply these verses to our scientific information. Our knowledge has so far encompassed only a very small part of this universe. Therefore we cannot say, as a matter of research, that this is the meaning of the Qur'an, and a human being cannot say this until he acquires all the knowledge of this universe. Hence we are content with the psychological aspect of this verse, namely that the commands of Allah encompass the entire universe.

This verse points to the entire universe: "Allah is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them." When a person reflects upon this, there rises before him the awe-inspiring and wondrous vastness of this universe: the expanse of Allah's dominion and the great signs of His power, in comparison with which this earth appears like a grain of mustard seed, and the creatures within it are even more insignificant, and their affairs more insignificant still. If in the universe of Allah the whole earth is a small ball, then what is the reality of the few coins that a husband spends and a wife receives?

Within this awe-inspiringly vast and wondrously great universe, the commands and orders of Allah operate. Marriage and divorce are a part of Allah's commands. Even from the standpoint of human knowledge, the commands of Allah that descend in this universe are greater than the measures of human conception. To oppose any command of Allah is, in effect, to invite the opposition of the entire universe. To invite the opposition of the heavens and the earth is a great audacity, and no intelligent person can commit such audacity, since the Messenger has come, reciting clear verses and bringing people out of darkness into light.

The meaning of the descent of Allah's commands in the heavens and the earth is that the conviction should be planted in the heart of the believer that Allah has power over all things. Therefore, nothing can prevent Him from whatever He wills. He knows everything; nothing is outside His knowledge. Everything is within His kingdom, and He also knows the secrets of hearts.

There are two aspects to this matter. One is that He who gives the family laws here has vast knowledge. Allah is aware of all circumstances, all benefits, and the limits of human capacity; therefore people should not deviate from Allah's commands even slightly, for it is a law made by the All-Knowing, the All-Encompassing.

The second is that these commands and their observance are left to your hearts and your consciences, and Allah knows your conscience and your awareness as well. Therefore, act upon these commands from the depths of your hearts with sincerity. Allah is not like the legislators of worldly laws who do not know; He is the Knower of what is in the breasts.

This surah concludes with this final note and the note of the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. Upon reflection a person is filled with awe, and has no recourse but to bow before Him and obey. Glory be to Allah; it is He who created hearts, and He alone knows the depths and heights of their valleys.
